newsitem.title: USA: Chicago City Council okays $3.77 bln FY 97 budget.
newsitem.headline: Chicago City Council okays $3.77 bln FY 97 budget.

text.p: The Chicago City Council on Wednesday approved a $3.77 billion budget for the fiscal year that begins Jan. 1.
On the new revenue front, the budget contained a 911 surcharge on cellular telephone users and a restructuring of parking tax rates to raise about $12 million a year.
Mayor Richard Daley proposed the budget last month saying that the spending plan emphasized improving neighborhoods.

While aldermen approved an increase in the property tax levy to support a capital improvement program for libraries, a vote on general obligation bond issuance for the library program and for $100 million of bonds for general city infrastructure projects is not expected until next month.
Daley had proposed a fiscal 1997 $150 million infrastructure bonding program that included $100 million of alternate bonds, mainly relying on city sales tax revenues for debt service payments.
The remaining $50 million of bonds, backed by revenues from the Chicago Skyway tollbridge are scheduled to be sold Thursday.

Walter Knorr, Chicago's chief financial officer, said the $100 million of alternate bonds, the $50 million of GO bonds for libraries, as well as $250 million of tender notes and $30 million of equipment notes should come up for final city council approval at the council's December meeting.
Knorr added that all the debt should be sold in the first quarter of 1997.

Goldman, Sachs & Co. has been tapped as senior manager for the alternate bonds, LaSalle Capital Markets for the library GO bonds, PaineWebber Inc for the tender notes and Reinoso & Co. for the equipment notes, according to Knorr.
In a published report last month, Moody's Investors Service called Daley's proposed budget "a reasonable operating plan for fiscal 1997."
Analysts from Standard & Poor's Corp. were not available to comment on the budget.
